svg.title: Eye trauma: look first for an open globe, then sort by mechanism. Surface and lid injuries are a metallic foreign body or a lid laceration; blunt trauma to the globe gives a hyphema or traumatic iritis; a stab or poke gives a corneal laceration with iris prolapse; each column gives the presentation, the exam finding and what to do

svg.text: Eye trauma: is the globe OPEN?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: look for: PEAKED pupil (in EVERY trauma) · Seidel sign · 360° subconjunctival hemorrhage · dark tissue at the limbus

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: (extruded uvea) · depth of the wound · shallow chamber

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: also: orbital rim pain or step-off · air under the skin · lid lacerations (full thickness? tear duct?) · forehead and cheek sensation

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: (V1, V2) · eye movements · proptosis or sunken eye
